speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry in light of the COVID-19 situation in China (a) whether the Ministry anticipates any disruptions in key supply chains for Singapore; (b) if so, which areas are expected to be harder hit; and (c) what measures are being taken to address these potential disruptions.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I note that we do not really anticipate any major disruptions, but I also would like to ask whether we do anticipate any short-term or medium-term price or financial impacts from any disruptions, short-term disruptions, out of this.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Like I have mentioned in my main answer, we have studied the situation very closely and in fact, since a few months back.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The current COVID-19 situation in China is still unfolding – like what Minister Ong Ye Kung and Minister Iswaran mentioned in their Ministerial Statements yesterday – as China continues to take steps to open their borders and transit to a new normal.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: MTI and all our economic agencies, including EDB, which is working with MNCs, with suppliers, with partners in China, as well as Enterprise Singapore working with Singapore companies with operations in China and also suppliers in China, we are working very closely with the companies via EDB, Enterprise Singapore and also the industry and trade association.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, we work very closely with companies with suppliers and operations in China and they shared with us that as they look into 2023, and as they look at the situation unfolding in China, they do not anticipate any major supply disruptions in China.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They shared that they have prepared for such scenarios because just like in the last three years, from time to time, as long as any province in China detect a COVID-19 situation, there will be a shutdown.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, they have prepared for such situations and they are fairly confident that they will be able to tide through this period.
